content.text: Attached sample files that can be used for testing, and test results on my host, with and without FeSL AuthZ enabled.
It's true that, according to RFC 2396: "scheme        = alpha *( alpha | digit | "+" | "-" | "." )" and:
"Scheme names consist of a sequence of characters beginning with a
lower case letter and followed by any combination of lower case
letters, digits, plus ("+"), period ("."), or hyphen ("-").  For
resiliency, programs interpreting URI should treat upper case letters
as equivalent to lower case in scheme names (e.g., allow "HTTP" as
well as "http")."
Is the PID supposed to be exposed as a URI attribute there, or is it a mistake not to ensure that it's prefixed with "info:fedora/"?
At a glance, it looks like legacy authZ doesn't populate this attribute.
It looks the PID should be supplied, and that it should be, but isn't, prefixed with "info:/fedora".
In org.fcrepo.server.security.xacml.pep.rest.objecthandlers.AddDatastream:

https://github.com/fcrepo/fcrepo/blob/f10c0986839eb75e5d18aba62c92e7fdf8182382/fcrepo-security/fcrepo-security-pep/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/server/security/xacml/pep/rest/objectshandlers/AddDatastream.java
Lines 82 - 85:
String path = request.getPathInfo();
String[] parts = path.split("/");
String pid = parts[1];
Lines 107 -110, where the error occurs:
if (pid != null && !"".equals(pid)) {
resAttr.put(new URI(XACML_RESOURCE_ID),
new AnyURIAttribute(new URI(pid)));

Lines 108, 120, and 124 (pid, formatURI, dsLocation) set a HashMap value to a URI, but don't check that the strings can actually be turned into URIs.  Perhaps some simple checks should be put into place there?  And the PID could definitely be first turned into a URI.

A more difficult question:  could we implement a check in the create object methods that verify these attributes can be populated (at least the ones that are common to all API actions, such as the PID), prior to ingesting the object, so we don't wind up in a situation where we create inaccessible objects?
https://github.com/fcrepo/fcrepo/commit/e0547ed724e52f1e57d13189bff3217e360ef99e

If the pid cannot be rendered as a URI, a warning is logged and the XACML machinery falls back to a string attribute.  This value is subsequently encoded with a leading slash, which makes the URI conversion work regardless.

When FeSL Authz is enabled, objects whose PIDs start with a digit cannot be accessed or modified once they are created.  The object is created, but attempts to view the object, add a datastream to it, or purge it result in this error:
java.net.URISyntaxException: Illegal character in scheme name at index 0
This exception appears to be thrown when URI.parse() is called in org.fcrepo.server.security.xacml.pep.rest.objectshandlers.GetObjectProfile.handleRequest().
Red Hat Enterprise Linux Server release 5.8 (Tikanga)
Linux 2.6.18-308.11.1.el5PAE #1 SMP i686 i386 GNU/Linux
Oracle Java 1.7.0_04
PostgreSQL 9.0.1
